newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Cadbury Nigeria ties profits to economy.
newsitem.headline: Cadbury Nigeria ties profits to economy.

text.p: Hopes of higher profits at consumer goods manufacturer Cadbury Nigeria Plc would depend on a healthier national economy, the company's chief executive said on Thursday.

Managing director Bunmi Oni, commenting on the company's half-year financial report in which it recorded a 15 percent rise in profit over 1996, said a similar growth should be expected provided there was no further economic downturn.
Cadbury said it netted 208.3 million naira in the half year to June 15, 1997 against 180.7 million naira a year earlier.
Oni said the feat was achieved against the backdrop of a contracting market, precipitated by Nigeria's economic depression.

"Markets have come down by between five percent and 25 percent recently," he told stock dealers and financial journalists at a forum in Lagos. "To say there has been a downturn is stating the obvious," he added.
Nigeria's economy has been sliding since 1993 after the military government annulled a presidential election which would have ushered civil democracy in Africa's most populous nation.
The presumed winner of the poll, businessman Moshood Abiola, has been detained since 1994 when he proclaimed himself president in defiance of the military rulers.
Most companies have been reporting falling profits as consumers' purchasing power has been progressively eroded by rising cost of living and inflation.
The Cadbury chief executive said the company's turnover for the period in review fell by 16 percent to 2.6 billion naira from 3.1 billion naira a year ago.
But the company managed to remain profitable because of an investment in information technology as well as other internal reorganisation, he said.
Cadbury shares were steady on Thursday at 35.60 naira.
Traders said the improved result announced helped to stem its current slide at Thursday's market although investors were still offloading the shares.
One said he would advise clients interested in income to buy the shares, adding: "It is no longer a growing stock."
In the year to end-1996, the company posted a profit after taxation of 823 million naira on an 8.2 billion naira turnover.
Profit after taxation was 605.9 million naira in 1995 when turnover touched 6.3 billion naira.
